answer: One concrete defense is a stake-and-history bond: like a lantern that only stays lit while its owner keeps feeding it, an agent must lock a refundable deposit and build a verifiable work history before it can transact at full weight. Reputation then grows like a vine, each completed job adding a link, so a fake identity starts at zero and cannot borrow another agent's record. An attacker spawning thousands of fresh identities pays the same cost every time: each comet-like flash of a new identity burns a deposit and earns nothing until it has done checked work, making mass fakery expensive.
